rationale: RFC_019 shipped a shared ResolvedAgentType ladder so the coordinator and the actions-package error-log door answer 'which agent is running' from one implementation instead of two that had drifted. Its section 7 declares, in the paper itself rather than leaving it to be discovered, a way that fix can be a PARTIAL NO-OP: rung 1 (RunAgentType) reaches an action unaided only on the first-step / same-message path, where the processor sets it and ToHeaders/FromHeaders carry it. A step RESUMED AFTER AN AWAIT rebuilds execCtx from the RESPONSE message's headers, which never carry RunAgentType, and ensureFullExecutionContext backfills Sender from state.OwnerAgentType but does not backfill its sibling at all. So for the rest of a resumed run every consumer of the ladder silently drops to rung 2 (the dispatch-path sender, often literally 'generic') while every existing test stays green. This submission is that declared follow-up. RFC_019 section 3 listed this exact edit in its alternatives table and DELIBERATELY DID NOT TAKE IT: 'Would probably make the fix land on resumed steps too (section 7), and is not taken here: it adds a rung sourced from durable state, which is a different claim needing its own evidence. Deliberately left as the named next round rather than bundled - this lane's round 2 was REJECTED for exactly that kind of bundling.' This is that round, pre-authorised by the owner on 2026-08-09 alongside the ruling that RFC_019's shared-ladder design ships (the round-1 guardian veto had routed the design choice to RFC_019 rather than to the gate, and the reuse_agent, constitution and architecture seats all argued for the shared ladder against the guardian's contained duplicate-it-locally alternative). The claim needing evidence is the SOURCE, and it is answerable from the code rather than by assertion: state.OwnerAgentType is determineOwnerAgentType's OWN durable output, written at run start from the same ladder (coordinator.go:661 assigns it; coordinator.go:1691 is where the actions door already consumes it as params.AgentType, which RFC_019 section 2 already reasoned is 'strictly more specific than the pod'). So this backfill does not invent a new authority or a new source of truth - it restores, on the resumed path, the answer the run already computed and persisted on its first step. ONE EDGE IS ACCEPTED AND DECLARED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: if resolution at run start bottomed out at determineOwnerAgentType's 'generic' filler, this backfill propagates that filler onto the resumed step's context. That is the ladder's own durable answer for that run, and it is no worse than today's behaviour, where the resumed step reads the dispatch-path Sender that is 'generic' on exactly the same paths. It cannot manufacture a WRONG specific agent type; the worst case is the value the run would have recorded anyway. Scope is deliberately one if-block plus tests: no new exported symbol, no schema, no config vocabulary, no wire-shape change, and no change to any consumer's fallback tail.

plan.summary: Close RFC_019 section 7's declared resumed-step gap with one guarded if-block in ensureFullExecutionContext: backfill execCtx.RunAgentType from state.OwnerAgentType (the ladder's own durable run-start output) when the rebuilt context has none, beside the Sender backfill that already does exactly this for its sibling field. Four table-driven cases pin it, two of them negative (a populated value is never overwritten; nothing is invented when state is empty too), and two mutations with disjoint failure sets prove the assignment and the guard separately. RFC_019 section 3 named this edit and deferred it to its own round rather than bundling it; this is that round.

edits.rationale: The fix. ensureFullExecutionContext already backfills Sender from state.OwnerAgentType when the rebuilt context has none; RunAgentType is its sibling and was never backfilled, which is the whole of RFC_019 section 7's declared limitation. Guarded on BOTH sides: it fires only when RunAgentType is empty (a message that carries its own resolved answer is more specific than the run-start record and must win) and only when state has an answer (so nothing is invented - an empty RunAgentType must fall through to the rungs below it, because handing the actions door a placeholder here would give it the 'generic' filler that RSH-008 chose 'unattributed' specifically to avoid colliding with). Sets updated=true so the existing log line reports it, matching every sibling block in the function.

Pins the resumed-step half of the ladder in the file that already pins the coordinator half, so a reader finds both consumers' proofs in one place. Four table-driven cases, and the two NEGATIVE ones are the load-bearing pair: 'a populated run agent type is never overwritten' is the guard, and 'nothing is invented when the state has no answer either' is the no-op case. The first case is deliberately shaped as the real resumed-step message - it carries a non-empty Sender ('generic'), so the pre-existing Sender backfill is a no-op on it, which is exactly what makes this distinct from the Sender fix and exactly why the gap was invisible. The fourth case asserts the two siblings still fire together when both are empty; it is what would catch the new block being written in place of the old one rather than beside it.

plan.risks: ACCEPTED AND DECLARED EDGE (the only behavioural one): if determineOwnerAgentType bottomed out at its 'generic' filler when the run started, state.OwnerAgentType holds 'generic' and this backfill propagates it onto the resumed step's context. That is the ladder's own durable answer for that run, and it is not a regression - today the resumed step reads execCtx.Sender.AgentType, which the Sender backfill immediately above sources from the SAME state.OwnerAgentType, so the value reaching a consumer is identical in that case. The backfill cannot manufacture a wrong SPECIFIC agent type: its only possible output is the value the run already computed and persisted. BLAST RADIUS: agent-chassis and every service built from it, write-path only, on the value of one column (agent_error_log.agent_type) on rows written through the six RSH-008 doors on the declared-inheritance path, and only on steps resumed after an await. orchestration_states.owner_agent_type is UNCHANGED - determineOwnerAgentType reads execCtx and is called before this function on the paths that set it, and in any case rung 1 and rung 2 now hold the same value wherever this fires, so its answer is identical for every input. RFC_019 section 4's consumer census applies unchanged and found NO automated consumer that branches on the value of that column: diagnose_load_runtime_action.go:265 renders it for display, reconcile_superseded_reviews_action.go:223 and page_build_failure_guard.go:131 filter on other columns, live agent config has 0 steps filtering on it, and sql_for_agents/214 selects it for display. The consumers are humans and the diagnosis bundle, through idx_error_log_agent. NOT AN ARCHITECTURE-SCOPE CHANGE, and the distinction is deliberate: RFC_019 was routed to the architecture track because it ADDED AN EXPORTED METHOD to types.ExecutionContext, which three packages import - the architecture seat's stated trigger, on the shape of the symbol and independent of blast radius. This change adds no exported symbol, changes no signature, adds no schema, no migration, no wire shape, no config vocabulary and no reserved key. It is an unexported function in one package gaining one guarded assignment from state it already reads four lines above. NO NEW AUTHORITY (the RFC_002 trigger): nothing can now refute, retract or re-type anything it could not before. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN HERE: the production claim. RFC_019 section 7 could not settle the resumed-step case by measurement because orchestration_states retains about 24 hours and every actions-door 'generic' row is older than that, so the join returns nothing to evaluate. That is unchanged and is stated rather than papered over - the decisive check is post-roll, and it is the check RFC_019 section 7 and the lane RUNBOOK already specify: count agent_error_log rows with agent_type='generic' for the three residual actions after the roll time, WITH the positive control alongside it, because a zero with no traffic is a dead path and not a fix. This change is inert until the next chassis roll. ROLLBACK is image-only: no schema, no config, no migration, and the previous binary tolerates every row this one writes.
grounded_in: RFC_019 section 7, the declared limitation: 'This may be a partial no-op on RESUMED steps, and it is stated here rather than left to be discovered. RunAgentType reaches the actions door on the first-step / same-message path (processor sets it -> ToHeaders -> FromHeaders -> buildActionParams hands the same execCtx to the action; the round trip is pinned by a test). On a step resumed after an await, execCtx is rebuilt from the RESPONSE message's headers, and ensureFullExecutionContext (coordinator.go:1589) backfills Sender from state.OwnerAgentType ONLY WHEN Sender IS EMPTY - it does not backfill RunAgentType at all.'

RFC_019 section 7, on why this is its own round and what the remedy is: 'I could not settle this by measurement: orchestration_states retains ~24h and every actions-door generic row is older than that, so the join returns nothing to evaluate. The decisive check is therefore post-roll, above. If the residue does not fall, the contained remedy is one if in ensureFullExecutionContext, and it belongs in its own round.'

RFC_019 section 3, alternatives table, the row that named this edit and deferred it: 'Backfill RunAgentType in ensureFullExecutionContext as well | Would probably make the fix land on resumed steps too (section 7), and is not taken here: it adds a rung sourced from durable state, which is a different claim needing its own evidence. Deliberately left as the named next round rather than bundled - this lane's round 2 was REJECTED for exactly that kind of bundling.'

coordinator.go:1589-1599, the sibling backfill this one sits beside and the reason the gap was invisible - it fires only on an EMPTY Sender, and a resumed response message carries one: 'if execCtx.Sender.AgentType == "" { execCtx.Sender = types.AgentIdentity{ AgentType: state.OwnerAgentType, AgentID: state.OwnerAgentID, PodName: podName, AgentVersion: os.Getenv("AGENT_VERSION"), Role: state.OwnerAgentRole, }; updated = true }'

types/context.go:62, the field's own doc comment, which is the contract this restores on the resumed path: 'RunAgentType is the RESOLVED real agent type whose workflow is executing (from config.agent_type / the loaded agent definition), as opposed to the dispatch-path sender which is often generic. Set by the processor before executing a workflow; consumed by the coordinator's determineOwnerAgentType so owner_agent_type records the real agent, not generic (bugs_open/060).'

coordinator.go:3466-3481, determineOwnerAgentType, showing that state.OwnerAgentType is this same ladder's own output and where the 'generic' filler the accepted edge refers to comes from: 'if agentType := execCtx.ResolvedAgentType(); agentType != "" { return agentType }; if agentType := os.Getenv("AGENT_TYPE"); agentType != "" { return agentType }; s.logger.Error("Did not find agent type in determineOwnerAgentType (coordinator 887)"); return "generic"'

RFC_019 section 2, on why state.OwnerAgentType is the right source rather than the pod environment: 'The actions door falls back to params.AgentType - which IS state.OwnerAgentType (coordinator.go:1691), this ladder's own durable output, so strictly more specific than the pod.'

RFC_019 section 10, bug_historian's note on this deferred gap: 'the declared resumed-step gap is structurally the shape of bugs_open/093 (one guarded call site, sibling path unchecked) and closed case 077 (detector wider than handler) ... disclosing and deferring it is the correct response to this pattern, not a violation of it, and it is non-regressive - resumed steps behave exactly as before.'

Mutation evidence for this change, run before submission (the lane's standard, RUNBOOK 'mutation harness' section). Mutation A, the whole if-block deleted: exactly two subtests fail - 'a resumed step gets the run's own resolved agent type back' and 'the two siblings are backfilled together when both are empty' - while the two negative subtests and all four pre-existing TestDetermineOwnerAgentType_Ladder subtests PASS, and nothing else in package orchestration fails. Mutation B, the emptiness guard dropped so the assignment becomes unconditional: exactly ONE subtest fails, 'a populated run agent type is never overwritten', and it is a DIFFERENT subtest from mutation A's pair. The two mutations fail disjoint sets, which is what distinguishes a test that pins the assignment from one that pins the guard.

Pre-existing test failures at committed HEAD, confirmed against a clean 'git archive HEAD' tree rather than assumed to be someone else's (RUNBOOK gotcha): TestValidDocSubjectTypes_LockstepWithMigrationCheck and TestEveryActionInputSpecHasARegistryEntry in platform/orchestration/actions, and TestEveryCheckProducedItemTypeIsClassified in platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks. Package platform/orchestration itself is 'ok' at baseline with this change applied.
